findings.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Public `findMany()` was removed and `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` return type changed from `Prisma...WhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, but this repo snapshot contains only `packages/lib` (no `apps/web`, `packages/trpc`, etc.), so any real caller (e.g. an insights tRPC router) that still calls `.findMany()` or spreads the old object-shaped conditions into a `where: {...}` cannot be located or verified as migrated, and the diff itself touches no caller files

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:106 — Column names/case-sensitive identifiers (`"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"`) are now hardcoded string literals in 6+ places, so a typo or future Prisma schema rename would only surface as a runtime SQL error instead of a compile-time TypeScript error.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:140 — The `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` in `buildAuthorizationConditions` is unreachable because `this.options.scope` is narrowed by the zod discriminated union to exactly `"user" \| "org" \| "team"`, all of which are already handled.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:49 — Entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block (2 tests) was deleted with no replacement, so `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization (still present in source at lines 49-50, 84, 91) now has zero test coverage

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:437 — Only the single "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test executes generated SQL via `prisma.$queryRaw`; team-scope (line 278), org-scope (line 305), and all filter-combo (lines 368-434) branches only assert `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` object shape and are never run against real data, so a query that is structurally "correct" per the test but invalid/wrong at execution time (bad quoting, wrong column, wrong join) would not be caught

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:210 — NOTHING_CONDITION (`Prisma.sql\`1=0\``) is only checked via structural `toEqual` at lines 210 and 245; no test actually runs a `$queryRaw` using this condition to confirm it returns zero rows end-to-end

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:273 — toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)` assertions only compare the `Sql` class's own enumerable `strings`/`values` arrays (verified in @prisma/client runtime: `sql`/`text`/`statement` are prototype getters, not own props), so they do meaningfully catch structural diffs in the literal template, but they require an exact whitespace-for-whitespace copy of the production template into the test (e.g. lines 296-298, 333-343), making these golden-copy duplication checks rather than independent behavioral verification, and they never prove the SQL is valid or executes correctly

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:166 — No test exercises the empty-array path for `ANY(${teamIds})`/`ANY(${userIds})` (e.g. an org/team with zero additional members) to confirm the code's guard (only pushing the array condition when non-empty) is actually load-bearing and would remain correct if that guard were removed

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332 — Org-scope test asserts exact array order of `teamIds`/`userIds` (e.g. `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`) coming from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`/`MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`; without a guaranteed ORDER BY this equality-by-position check risks flakiness if the DB doesn't return rows in insertion order

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Public `findMany()` was removed and `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` return type changed from `Prisma...WhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, but this repo snapshot contains only `packages/lib` (no `apps/web`, `packages/trpc`, etc.), so any real caller (e.g. an insights tRPC router) that still calls `.findMany()` or spreads the old object-shaped conditions into a `where: {...}` cannot be located or verified as migrated, and the diff itself touches no caller files

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` and changes `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()` to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `Prisma...WhereInput` (see `insightsBooking.ts`, replacing `findMany` with `getBaseConditions` and updating cached types). This is an API-breaking change for any external callers that previously invoked `.findMany()` or used the object-shaped `where` inputs; the diff itself only updates integration tests and does not show any migrations in other potential call sites. However, whether any such callers exist/break cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:106 — Column names/case-sensitive identifiers (`"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"`) are now hardcoded string literals in 6+ places, so a typo or future Prisma schema rename would only surface as a runtime SQL error instead of a compile-time TypeScript error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Prisma typed `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` objects with `Prisma.sql` fragments (e.g. `Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${...})`, `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"` in `buildAuthorizationConditions`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`, and `buildFilterConditions`). These quoted column identifiers are now hardcoded strings, so schema/field renames or typos won’t be caught by TypeScript/Prisma typing and would fail at runtime when executing the raw SQL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:140 — The `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` in `buildAuthorizationConditions` is unreachable because `this.options.scope` is narrowed by the zod discriminated union to exactly `"user" \| "org" \| "team"`, all of which are already handled.

adjudication.rationale: In `buildAuthorizationConditions`, `this.options.scope` is indeed limited to "user" | "org" | "team" after `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(options)` (and invalid values would throw before this method runs), so the trailing `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` is redundant/unreachable. However, this is just a minor cleanup/nit and not a defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:49 — Entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block (2 tests) was deleted with no replacement, so `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization (still present in source at lines 49-50, 84, 91) now has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` (two tests), and there is no new/alternative test added that exercises the memoization behavior. In `insightsBooking.ts`, caching still exists via `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` and the `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()` getters that populate them only when `=== undefined`. Other remaining tests call these methods but only once per test, so they don't verify caching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:437 — Only the single "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test executes generated SQL via `prisma.$queryRaw`; team-scope (line 278), org-scope (line 305), and all filter-combo (lines 368-434) branches only assert `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` object shape and are never run against real data, so a query that is structurally "correct" per the test but invalid/wrong at execution time (bad quoting, wrong column, wrong join) would not be caught

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites most assertions in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` to `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)`, which only checks the constructed `Prisma.Sql` object (template/values) rather than executing it. Only the renamed `getBaseConditions` test actually runs SQL via `prisma.$queryRaw` with `WHERE ${baseConditions}`. So team-scope/org-scope authorization and the filter-only / filter-combo branches are not validated against real query execution and could miss runtime SQL issues (e.g., invalid column names/quoting) introduced by the new raw-SQL construction in `insightsBooking.ts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:210 — NOTHING_CONDITION (`Prisma.sql\`1=0\``) is only checked via structural `toEqual` at lines 210 and 245; no test actually runs a `$queryRaw` using this condition to confirm it returns zero rows end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the service to return `Prisma.Sql` conditions (e.g. `const NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0``) that are intended to be interpolated into `$queryRaw` (see new `getBaseConditions()` and the updated integration test at the end using `WHERE ${baseConditions}`). However, the two tests that cover the “nothing” cases (`should return NOTHING for non-admin user` and `should return NOTHING for non-owner/admin user`) only assert `expect(conditions).toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION)` and never execute a query using that condition to prove it filters to zero rows end-to-end. Given the shift from Prisma `where` objects to raw SQL snippets, an end-to-end query assertion for the NOTHING case would specifically validate the new behavior rather than just structural equality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:273 — toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)` assertions only compare the `Sql` class's own enumerable `strings`/`values` arrays (verified in @prisma/client runtime: `sql`/`text`/`statement` are prototype getters, not own props), so they do meaningfully catch structural diffs in the literal template, but they require an exact whitespace-for-whitespace copy of the production template into the test (e.g. lines 296-298, 333-343), making these golden-copy duplication checks rather than independent behavioral verification, and they never prove the SQL is valid or executes correctly

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the service to return `Prisma.Sql` fragments (e.g. `buildAuthorizationConditions`, `buildFilterConditions`) and updates tests to assert `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)`. Those assertions necessarily encode the exact SQL template output (including parentheses/whitespace/layout) rather than independently verifying behavior, making the tests brittle to harmless formatting refactors (e.g. the long OR/ANY templates in the org/team scope expectations). Also, aside from the single `getBaseConditions` test that actually runs `$queryRaw`, most tests only compare the `Sql` object structure and don’t validate that the produced SQL executes correctly against the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:166 — No test exercises the empty-array path for `ANY(${teamIds})`/`ANY(${userIds})` (e.g. an org/team with zero additional members) to confirm the code's guard (only pushing the array condition when non-empty) is actually load-bearing and would remain correct if that guard were removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the service to build raw SQL with `ANY(${...})` and explicitly guards only the `userIds`-based branches: in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` it only adds the `("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})) ...` clause when `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0`, and in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` it only adds the `ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` clause when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`. The updated integration tests assert SQL for cases where those arrays are non-empty, but none exercise the “no additional members / empty userIds array” path to ensure the guard is needed and stays correct. (The finding’s mention of an empty `teamIds` path is less grounded because org `teamIds` always includes `options.orgId`, but the missing coverage for empty `userIds` arrays is real and diff-specific.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332 — Org-scope test asserts exact array order of `teamIds`/`userIds` (e.g. `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`) coming from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`/`MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`; without a guaranteed ORDER BY this equality-by-position check risks flakiness if the DB doesn't return rows in insertion order

adjudication.rationale: In the org-scope integration test, the expected condition is built as a `Prisma.sql` with `ANY(${[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]})` and similarly for userIds. In the implementation, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` constructs `teamIds` via `teamsFromOrg.map((t) => t.id)` and user IDs via repository results, with no sorting/ORDER BY shown in the diff. Since the test asserts exact structural equality of the `Prisma.Sql` (including parameter array ordering), it can fail if repositories return rows in a different order, even though SQL semantics of `= ANY(array)` are order-insensitive. This is a real flakiness risk in the test, not a production bug.
